summary: Taiken Tanaka is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Hiroshima University. In 1991, he was attested as an assistant professor at Aichi Gakuin University.
Taiki Mibu is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Ryukoku University by 2016. In 2015, Mibu was attested as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University.

Taikyo Tanigawa is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who completed doctoral coursework at Koyasan University and earned a Ph.D. from Toyo University in 1994. He served as assistant professor (attested 1980–1988) and professor (attested 2005) at Koyasan University.
Taion Satomi is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University from around 1930 to 1933. In 1972, he was attested as a professor at Minobusan Junior College.

Taira Shidehara (1870–1953) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Sinology who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1893–1896). He later held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1900–1906) and Tokyo University of Education (~1900–1919).
Tairyu Tsunoda is a Buddhist studies scholar. He was attested as a lecturer at Komazawa Junior College in 1995 and as a professor at Komazawa University in 2015.
Taisei Iwata is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He was attested as a lecturer at Rissho University in 1984 and as a professor at Otani University in 1996.
Taisen Deshimaru (1914–1982) worked in Buddhist and religious studies, studying under teacher Kodo Sawaki from around 1936 to 1965. He founded the Association Zen Internationale and La Gendronnière.

Taishu Tagami is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo (~1959–1962). He served as professor at Komazawa University (~1978–2006) and concurrent lecturer at the Eastern Institute (attested 1990).

Taishun Mibu (1913–1980) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Taisho University (~1934–1937). He served as director at Taisho University (~1963–1979) and taught Ryusho Onami.

Taitetsu Unno (1929–2014) was a Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy scholar who studied at UC Berkeley (~1947–1951) and the University of Tokyo (~1951–1968). He taught Leo M. Pruden and Jeff Wilson, and served as Jill Ker Conway Professor Emeritus of Religion at Smith College (1971–1998).

Taitsu Kono is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Hanazono University and under Mumon Yamada (~1954–1988). He succeeded Sōkō Morinaga (attested 1995) and served as president of Hanazono University (~1990–2000).

Taixu (1890–1947) worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy, studying under Jichan, Jingan, and Yang Renshan. He founded multiple institutions—including Wuchang Buddhist Institute, Minnan Buddhist Institute, and Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Institute—and led Minnan Buddhist Institute (1927).

Taizan Maezumi (1931–1995) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Komazawa University, Soji-ji, and SFSU, and trained under Baian Hakujun Kuroda, Koryu Osaka, and Hakuun Ryōko Yasutani. He founded the Zen Center of Los Angeles, Kuroda Institute, and White Plum Asanga.
Tak Pui Sze is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies who earned a PhD at the University of British Columbia, where doctoral supervision was provided by Jinhua Chen.

Taka Yanagisawa (1926–2003) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Japan Women's University. She taught Anne Nishimura Morse and served as Director of the Department of Fine Arts at Tokyo National Research Institute for Cultural Properties (~1982–1989).
Takahiko Kameyama is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. In 2015, Kameyama was attested as a professor at the Institute of Buddhist Studies and as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University.

Takamaro Shigaraki (1926–2014) was a Buddhist studies scholar who completed degrees at Ryukoku University, later serving there as faculty (1958), professor (1970), and president (1989–1995). He also chaired the Society for the Promotion of Buddhism and Bukkyō Dendō Kyōkai.

Takamatsu Yoshie (1880–1940) studied at Tōkyō Senmon Gakkō, Waseda University, and the University of Paris. He served at Waseda University as lecturer (1908, 1910), professor (1915), and Dean of Letters (1930), and also taught Kangei Okamoto.

Takami Inoue is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. Inoue was a doctoral candidate at the University of California, Santa Barbara (attested 2003) and served as Professor of Shin Buddhist Studies at Otani University.
